mn_harsenville.title: Upper_West_Side
mn_harsenville.note: Hamlet on the Bloomingdale Road around today's 71st Street, named for the Harsen family farm. Start and end years estimated.

si_stony_brook.title: Staten_Island
si_stony_brook.note: First seat of Richmond County, from 1683 until the courts moved to Richmond Town about 1729. Start and end years estimated. Location approximate (Amboy Road near Richmond Road, today's Egbertville).

si_richmond.note: County seat from about 1729 (Richmond Town); year estimated.

si_oude_dorp.note: First lasting European settlement, August 1661, near today's South Beach; location approximate (the only surviving building of the colony, the Billiou-Stillwell-Perine House of 1662, stands 2.6 km inland on Richmond Road). End year estimated.

bx_unionport.note: Village laid out in the 1850s; year estimated.

qn_douglaston.note: The railway arrived in 1866 and the stop was named for William Douglas, who gave the station building; year estimated.

mn_washington_market.note: Wholesale market district on the lower west side, opened 1813 as Bear Market; the market moved to Hunts Point in 1967 (end year estimated).

mn_carnegie_hill.note: Named for the mansion Andrew Carnegie built in 1901 at Fifth Avenue and 91st Street.

mn_little_oyster_island.note: Dutch-period name (bought by Michael Paauw 1630). End year estimated.

mn_fort_william.note: Fort William under Leisler from 1689, then Fort William Henry. End year estimated.

mn_fort_anne.note: Named for Queen Anne (reigned 1702-1714); years estimated from the reign.

mn_fort_george.note: Named for George I (from 1714, year estimated); demolished 1790 for Government House.

mn_harlem_town.note: English-period village (an attempt to rename it Lancaster failed). End year estimated: Harlem was built into the city in the 1870s.

mn_harlem.note: Neighbourhood label at 125th Street and Lenox Avenue. Start year estimated.

bk_brownsville.note: Named for Charles S. Brown, who subdivided the land in the 1860s; year estimated.

bk_bushwick_town.note: Town of Kings County; merged into the City of Brooklyn with Williamsburgh by the act of 1854, in effect 1 Jan 1855. Name switch from Boswijck dated to the English takeover of 1664 (nominal).

qn_maspat.note: Rev. Francis Doughty's English settlement of 1642, the first in Queens, destroyed in Kieft's War; end year estimated.

qn_middelburgh.note: Town founded 1652; label at the old village (Broadway and Queens Boulevard). Renaming year estimated.

qn_newtown.note: Renamed New Towne after the English takeover (year estimated); town of Queens County.

qn_dominies_hook.note: Land granted to Dominie Everardus Bogardus in the 1640s; start year estimated.

qn_rego_park.note: Named for the Real Good Construction Company, which built here in the 1920s; year estimated.

qn_richmond_hill.note: Laid out by Albon Platt Man about 1868-1869; year estimated.

qn_college_point.note: Named for St. Paul's College (1835); village incorporated in the late 1860s, year estimated.

qn_strattonport.note: Village laid out on the Stratton farm; start and end years estimated.

qn_whitestone.note: Settled in the 1640s and named for a white boulder on the shore; start year estimated.

qn_laurelton.note: Laurelton Land Company development of the 1900s; year estimated.

qn_cambria_heights.note: Developed in the 1920s with financing from the Cambria Title Savings and Trust Company; year estimated.

qn_far_rockaway.note: Resort from the Marine Pavilion of the 1830s; start year estimated.

qn_arverne.note: Developed by Remington Vernam in the late 1880s; year estimated.

qn_broad_channel.note: Fishing and railway village on the Jamaica Bay trestle, from about 1880; year estimated.

bx_morrisania_town.note: Morris family estate from about 1670 (start year estimated), manor 1697; village of Morrisania founded 1848, town 1855; annexed to New York 1874.

bx_west_farms_town.note: Patent of 1666 to Edward Jessup and John Richardson (land bought 1663); town 1846-1874.

bx_cornells_neck.note: Thomas Cornell's grant of the 1640s; start and end years estimated.

bx_hunts_point.note: Named for Thomas Hunt, who settled here in the 1660s; year estimated.

bx_woodlawn.note: Laid out in the 1870s by George Opdyke; year estimated.

bx_catholic_protectory.note: New York Catholic Protectory, on this site from 1865; the land was sold to Metropolitan Life in the late 1930s, end year estimated.

bx_eastchester.note: Southern end of the colonial town of Eastchester (the Ten Farms of the 1660s); start year estimated.

si_clifton.note: Laid out in the late 1830s; year estimated.

si_arrochar.note: Named for the estate W. W. MacFarland established in the 1840s; neighbourhood from the 1880s, year estimated.

si_factoryville.note: Named for the dye works of 1819; start and end years estimated.

si_linoleumville.note: Named for the American Linoleum Manufacturing Company plant of 1873; end year estimated.

si_travis.note: Residents voted to rename the village about 1930, after the plant closed; year estimated.

si_prohibition_park.note: The Prohibition Campground Association bought its first 25 acres in 1877; end year estimated.

si_kreischerville.note: Balthasar Kreischer's brickworks village, from 1854; end year estimated.

ls_harlem_river.note: Named for Nieuw Haarlem (1658); Lenape Muscoota. Start year nominal.

ls_gravesend_bay.note: Named for the town (1645); start year nominal.
